weeks.title: Follow up with warm prospects
weeks.description: A tiny execution rep that keeps lead generation moving without feeling heavy.
weeks.action: Send 5 follow-up messages to people who ghosted your value session invite.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Ignore cold outreach for this week.

Open your CRM or message thread list and find five people who showed interest, then went quiet after a value-session invite.

Write a short, specific follow-up. One clear reason to reconnect. One easy next step.

weeks.title: Sharpen your positioning
weeks.description: Use one small prompt to improve how clearly prospects understand what you do.
weeks.action: Update one line in your LinkedIn headline so it speaks more directly to your core client.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Do not rewrite your whole profile.

Change one line so a stranger instantly understands who you help and the outcome you create.

If it still sounds generic, make it more specific.

weeks.title: Tighten your booking messages
weeks.description: Small messaging tweaks compound fast when you are booking value sessions every week.
weeks.action: Rewrite one invite or reminder message so it sounds more specific, personal, and easy to reply to.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Pick your weakest invite or reminder.

Make it shorter. Make the next step obvious. Make it feel like it was written for one person, not a list.

weeks.title: Reinforce one client habit
weeks.description: A fast coaching rep that strengthens delivery quality without needing a full planning session.
weeks.action: Add one metric to a client dashboard and commit to reviewing it with them in your next session.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Choose one number that actually changes behaviour.

Add it to the dashboard. Tell the client you will review it together next session. Keep the conversation on that one habit.

weeks.title: Clean your prospect list
weeks.description: A short list-quality rep that improves every conversation you start this month.
weeks.action: Remove 10 weak prospects from your active list and replace them with 10 stronger ones.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Your list quality sets the ceiling for your outreach.

Cut anyone who is not a real fit. Add ten people who match your core client more closely.

weeks.title: Prep one value session
weeks.description: A practical sales rep that makes your next value session feel sharper and more useful.
weeks.action: Spend 15 minutes preparing one upcoming value session with three questions and one clear outcome.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Write three discovery questions.

Decide the one outcome you want them to leave with.

Then run the session against that plan, not against improvisation.

weeks.title: Close the loop on actions
weeks.description: A delivery discipline rep that stops coaching from becoming interesting conversation with no follow-through.
weeks.action: Review last session’s action list with one client and confirm what actually got done.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Open the last coaching sheet.

Ask what moved. Ask what stalled. Reset one next action that is clear enough to complete this week.

weeks.title: Start five new conversations
weeks.description: A simple pipeline rep. Volume only matters when the messages are personal.
weeks.action: Start 5 new conversations with people on your Top 100 list.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
No batch spam.

Five personal openings. Mention something specific. Ask one easy question that invites a reply.

weeks.title: Practise your pitch transition
weeks.description: A short sales-skill rep that makes the move into the offer feel natural instead of abrupt.
weeks.action: Practise your value-session-to-pitch transition out loud once, then refine one sentence.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Record yourself or say it out loud once.

If the transition feels forced, rewrite the bridging sentence until it sounds like the natural next step.

weeks.title: Improve one session opening
weeks.description: A delivery polish rep. Better openings create better sessions.
weeks.action: Rewrite your first 2 minutes of a coaching session so they start with progress, energy, and one clear focus.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Cut the warm-up waffle.

Open with progress since last time, current energy, and the one issue that matters most today.

weeks.title: Fix your calendar friction
weeks.description: A tiny systems rep that removes one reason prospects do not book.
weeks.action: Check your booking link and availability, then remove one piece of friction that makes scheduling harder than it needs to be.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Click your own booking link.

If it feels confusing, slow, or scarce, fix one thing: clearer times, fewer steps, or a cleaner confirmation message.

weeks.title: Ask for one decision
weeks.description: A closing discipline rep. Soft conversations still need a clear next step.
weeks.action: On your next value session or sales call, ask for one clear decision before you end.
weeks.bodyMarkdown:
Do not leave the call in a vague maybe.

Ask for the next step: book the sales call, start, or decide not to. Clarity helps both of you.
